act.title_original: Bundesgesetz über Barrierefreiheitsanforderungen für Produkte und Dienstleistungen (Barrierefreiheitsgesetz – BaFG)
act.title_en: Federal Act on accessibility requirements for products and services (Accessibility Act – BaFG)

authority_ecommerce.name_en: Federal Office for Social Affairs and Disability (Sozialministeriumservice)
authority_ecommerce.basis: § 21 BaFG (competence), § 28 (measures for services), § 36 (penalties imposed by the Sozialministeriumservice)

penalties.summary_en: Offering or providing a service contrary to § 14(1) is punishable by up to EUR 80,000 (up to EUR 50,000 for SMEs); failing to draw up the Annex 3 information up to EUR 40,000 (EUR 25,000 for SMEs); failing to provide/keep the information, notify non-conformity or cooperate up to EUR 16,000.

accessibility_information.where: general terms and conditions or a similar document
accessibility_information.basis: § 14(2) BaFG; Anlage 3 Z 1 BaFG (information to be made available to the public in written and oral form, including in an accessible format)

microenterprise_exemption.basis: § 6(1) BaFG (microenterprises offering or providing services are exempt from the § 4(3) requirements and all related obligations); definition § 3 Z 19

transition: Service providers may keep using products lawfully used before 28 June 2025 until 28 June 2030, and service contracts agreed before 28 June 2025 may continue unchanged until expiry but no longer than five years from that date (§ 37(2) BaFG).
notes: BaFG has no implementing ordinance: the accessibility requirements are in Anlage 1 of the Act itself. Before issuing an order the Sozialministeriumservice must first ask the provider to take corrective action within a set deadline (§ 28(1) Z 1 BaFG). Consumers and VKI, Behindertenrat, Arbeiterkammer and WKO may report breaches (§ 35). Fines go to the Unterstützungsfonds für Menschen mit Behinderungen (§ 36(5)). The consolidated RIS page blocks automated clients; the text was read per paragraph from the RIS OGD API (all paragraphs in the version of BGBl. I Nr. 76/2023, no amendments listed as of 2026-09-25).

act.title_original: Loi du 5 novembre 2023 modifiant plusieurs livres du Code de droit économique et la loi du 2 août 2002 relative à la surveillance du secteur financier et aux services financiers en vue de la transposition partielle de la directive (UE) 2019/882 du Parlement européen et du Conseil du 17 avril 2019 relative aux exigences en matière d'accessibilité applicables aux produits et services, pour ce qui concerne certains services
act.title_en: Act of 5 November 2023 amending several books of the Code of Economic Law and the Act of 2 August 2002 on the supervision of the financial sector and financial services, for the partial transposition of Directive (EU) 2019/882 on accessibility requirements for products and services, as regards certain services
act.citation: M.B./B.S. 28.11.2023, numac 2023046827; inserts Code de droit économique Book VIII, Title 5 (art. VIII.58–VIII.66, annexes 1–4) and art. XV.18/5–XV.18/7, XV.62/7, XV.101/1

authority_ecommerce.name_original: SPF Economie, P.M.E., Classes moyennes et Énergie – Direction générale de l'Inspection économique
authority_ecommerce.name_en: FPS Economy, SMEs, Self-employed and Energy – Directorate-General Economic Inspection
authority_ecommerce.basis: CDE art. XV.2 agents (referred to in art. VIII.59 §3, VIII.61 §2–3, VIII.62, XV.18/5); SPF Economie press release of 2 July 2025 names the Inspection économique as competent for e-commerce services

penalties.type: criminal fine (sanction de niveau 2 / niveau 3), may be settled by administrative fine
penalties.summary_en: Breaches of art. VIII.59–VIII.62 (accessibility requirements, information, conformity procedures, disproportionate-burden assessment) are punished with a level-2 sanction (EUR 26–10,000 or 4% of annual turnover if higher), or level 3 in bad faith (EUR 26–25,000 or 6% of annual turnover if higher); the court may add corrective measures.
penalties.basis: CDE art. XV.101/1, XV.70 §1, 2° and 3° (as replaced by the Act of 8 May 2022), XV.132, XV.62/7

accessibility_information.basis: CDE art. VIII.60 and annex 2 to Book VIII (information to be made public in written and oral form, including in an accessible way, kept as long as the service is available)

microenterprise_exemption.basis: Art. 40 of the Act of 5 November 2023: undertakings with fewer than 10 employees and annual turnover or balance sheet total ≤ EUR 2,000,000 are excluded from the Act until 28 June 2030 (temporary); CDE art. VIII.59 §2 allows the King to exclude micro-enterprises from some or all requirements

transition: Service contracts agreed before 28 June 2025 may run unchanged until expiry, at most five years; products lawfully used before that date may be used until 28 June 2030 (art. 39); for micro-enterprises the whole Act applies only from 28 June 2030, with contracts running up to five years further and product use until 28 June 2035 (art. 40); complaints about facts before 28 June 2025 (before 28 June 2030 for micro-enterprises) are inadmissible (CDE art. XV.18/5 §3, 2°).
notes: Belgian official portals (ejustice.just.fgov.be, economie.fgov.be, lachambre.be) blocked automated access during verification. The Act's text was read from the etaamb.openjustice.be copy of the Moniteur belge (which says it is not the official version); the official Justel link is given as act.url. Annex 2 (the information template) is published only as an image and was NOT read, so 'accessibility_information.where' is null; a search-engine snippet of Justel suggests 'clauses et conditions générales ou dans un document équivalent' (matching Directive Annex V), but this is unverified. XV.70 amounts come from the Act of 8 May 2022 (numac 2022041208, etaamb copy); later amendments to XV.70 were not checked. The amounts exclude the décimes additionnels (currently ×8, a figure not checked in the statute). The SPF Economie press release (2 July 2025) says penalties reach EUR 200,000 or 6% of annual turnover for the most serious breaches, which matches EUR 25,000 × 8. The micro-enterprise exclusion is temporary (until 28 June 2030), unlike DE/AT/NL. No royal decree specific to e-commerce services was found, but this could not be fully checked because the portals were blocked.

act.title_original: Ο περί της Προσβασιμότητας Προϊόντων και Υπηρεσιών Νόμος του 2024, Ν. 57(Ι)/2024
act.title_en: Accessibility of Products and Services Law of 2024, L. 57(I)/2024
act.citation: Official Gazette, Annex I, Part I, No. 4996, 2 May 2024

penalties.type: administrative fine; also a criminal offence
penalties.summary_en: Administrative fine up to EUR 10,000 (EUR 20,000 for a repeat breach) plus up to EUR 500 per day while it continues; as a criminal offence up to EUR 20,000 and/or 2 years (repeat: EUR 30,000 and/or 3 years).

notes: Market-surveillance departments are to be designated by the Council of Ministers (art. 3(3)); that decision was not checked.

act.title_original: Zákon č. 424/2023 Sb., o požadavcích na přístupnost některých výrobků a služeb
act.title_en: Act No. 424/2023 Coll. on accessibility requirements for certain products and services

penalties.summary_en: Up to CZK 10,000,000 for a service that does not meet the requirements, is not fixed, or ignores ordered measures; lower caps (CZK 5M / 2M / 1M) for other service offences, CZK 1M for not publishing the § 14 information.

accessibility_information.where: general terms or equivalent document (also in audio form on request)

transition: Services under contracts concluded before the act took effect may continue unchanged until the contract ends, at the latest 28 June 2030 (§ 28).

act.title_original: Gesetz zur Umsetzung der Richtlinie (EU) 2019/882 des Europäischen Parlaments und des Rates über die Barrierefreiheitsanforderungen für Produkte und Dienstleistungen (Barrierefreiheitsstärkungsgesetz – BFSG)
act.title_en: Act implementing Directive (EU) 2019/882 of the European Parliament and of the Council on the accessibility requirements for products and services (Accessibility Strengthening Act – BFSG)
act.citation: BGBl. I 2021 S. 2970 (16 July 2021), last amended by Art. 32 of the Act of 6 May 2024 (BGBl. 2024 I Nr. 149)

secondary_acts.title_original: Verordnung über die Barrierefreiheitsanforderungen für Produkte und Dienstleistungen nach dem Barrierefreiheitsstärkungsgesetz (Verordnung zum Barrierefreiheitsstärkungsgesetz – BFSGV)
secondary_acts.citation: BGBl. I 2022 S. 928 (15 June 2022), amended by Art. 1 of the Ordinance of 10 July 2026 (BGBl. 2026 I Nr. 205)

secondary_acts.title_original: Staatsvertrag zur Aufgabenerfüllung nach dem Barrierefreiheitsstärkungsgesetz vom 5. März 2025
secondary_acts.citation: Interstate treaty of the 16 Länder (e.g. Brandenburg GVBl. I/25 Nr. 9); in force 26 September 2025

authority_ecommerce.name_original: Marktüberwachungsstelle der Länder für die Barrierefreiheit von Produkten und Dienstleistungen (MLBF AöR), Magdeburg
authority_ecommerce.name_en: Market Surveillance Authority of the Länder for the Accessibility of Products and Services (MLBF), Magdeburg
authority_ecommerce.basis: §§ 20, 28–31 BFSG (market surveillance is a Länder task); Art. 2–3 Staatsvertrag zur Aufgabenerfüllung nach dem BFSG (joint public-law institution, seat in Saxony-Anhalt, takes over all tasks the BFSG assigns to the Länder market surveillance authorities)

penalties.summary_en: Offering or providing an e-commerce service contrary to § 14(1) (not meeting the BFSGV requirements, or without the Annex 3 information made accessible to the public) is a regulatory offence punishable by a fine of up to EUR 100,000; other service-provider offences (e.g. failing to notify non-conformity under § 14(4) or to give information to the authority under § 14(5)) up to EUR 10,000.

accessibility_information.where: general terms and conditions (Allgemeine Geschäftsbedingungen) or in another clearly perceptible manner
accessibility_information.basis: § 14(1) Nr. 2 BFSG; Anlage 3 Nr. 1 BFSG (elements a–d, incl. naming the competent market surveillance authority)

microenterprise_exemption.basis: § 3(3) BFSG (requirements of § 3(1) do not apply to microenterprises offering or providing services); definition § 2 Nr. 17 BFSG (<10 persons and annual turnover or balance sheet total ≤ EUR 2 million)

transition: Service providers may keep using products lawfully used before 28 June 2025 until 27 June 2030, and service contracts concluded before 28 June 2025 may continue unchanged until they expire, at most until 27 June 2030 (§ 38(1) BFSG); no general grace period for the e-commerce service itself.
notes: § 2 Nr. 26 BFSG defines 'Dienstleistungen im elektronischen Geschäftsverkehr' by reference to digital services under § 1(4) Nr. 1 Digitale-Dienste-Gesetz. E-commerce-specific requirements are in § 19 BFSGV. The BFSGV amendment of 10 July 2026 (BGBl. 2026 I Nr. 205) reportedly revised §§ 7 and 14 BFSGV (self-service terminals, emergency communication), according to secondary sources; the amending text itself was not read, and § 19 BFSGV (e-commerce) reads the same in the current consolidated version. The MLBF started work when the Staatsvertrag entered into force on 26 Sept 2025 (Schleswig-Holstein government page); before that date supervision rested with individual Länder. The MLBF's own website refused connections during verification, so its URL and address (Carl-Miller-Straße 6, 39112 Magdeburg) were taken from the Schleswig-Holstein government page.

act.title_original: Lov nr. 801 af 7. juni 2022 om tilgængelighedskrav for produkter og tjenester
act.title_en: Act No. 801 of 7 June 2022 on accessibility requirements for products and services
act.citation: Lovtidende A, 7 June 2022; amended by lov nr. 637 af 11. juni 2024

penalties.summary_en: Breaches, including the service provider's information duty, are punishable by a fine set by the courts; companies can be held liable. The act sets no amount.

accessibility_information.where: general terms or equivalent document, in writing and orally

transition: Service contracts concluded before 28 June 2025 may run until they expire, at the latest 28 June 2030 (§ 59).

act.title_original: Ley 11/2023, de 8 de mayo, de trasposición de Directivas de la Unión Europea en materia de accesibilidad de determinados productos y servicios, migración de personas altamente cualificadas, tributaria y digitalización de actuaciones notariales y registrales; y por la que se modifica la Ley 12/2011, de 27 de mayo, sobre responsabilidad civil por daños nucleares o producidos por materiales radiactivos (título I)
act.title_en: Law 11/2023 of 8 May transposing European Union Directives on the accessibility of certain products and services, migration of highly qualified persons, taxation and digitalisation of notarial and registry procedures; and amending Law 12/2011 of 27 May on civil liability for nuclear damage or damage caused by radioactive materials (Title I)
act.citation: BOE núm. 110, de 9 de mayo de 2023 (BOE-A-2023-11022)

secondary_acts.title_original: Real Decreto 143/2026, de 25 de febrero, por el que se crea y regula la Unidad técnica de apoyo y coordinación de las autoridades de vigilancia en materia de requisitos de accesibilidad
secondary_acts.citation: BOE núm. 52, de 27 de febrero de 2026 (BOE-A-2026-4520)

secondary_acts.title_original: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2013, de 29 de noviembre, por el que se aprueba el Texto Refundido de la Ley General de derechos de las personas con discapacidad y de su inclusión social (título III, supletorio)
secondary_acts.citation: BOE núm. 289, de 3 de diciembre de 2013 (BOE-A-2013-12632)

authority_ecommerce.name_original: Autoridades de vigilancia designadas por las comunidades autónomas y las ciudades de Ceuta y Melilla; en su defecto, la Unidad técnica de apoyo y coordinación (UTAC), Dirección General de Derechos de las Personas con Discapacidad
authority_ecommerce.name_en: Surveillance authorities designated by each autonomous community (and Ceuta/Melilla); where none is designated, the Technical Support and Coordination Unit (UTAC) of the Directorate-General for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
authority_ecommerce.basis: Ley 11/2023 art. 27.3 and art. 28.2 g); Real Decreto 143/2026 arts. 2 and 3 h)

penalties.summary_en: Ley 11/2023 sets no fines of its own: breaches are punished under the applicable sectoral regime and, failing that, under Title III of RDL 1/2013, where failure to meet accessibility requirements is a serious infringement (EUR 30,001–90,000 at State level) or, where it prevents free access and use, a very serious one (up to EUR 1,000,000); autonomous communities type the infringements in their own legislation.

accessibility_information.basis: Ley 11/2023 art. 13.2 (« en las condiciones generales o documento equivalente ») and 13.4

transition: Until 28 June 2030 providers may keep providing services with products lawfully used before that date, and service contracts concluded before 28 June 2025 may continue unchanged until expiry but not beyond five years from that date (disposición transitoria única, apdo. 1).
notes: max_amount is the absolute ceiling of RDL 1/2013 art. 83.1 (very serious infringements); art. 83.3 caps serious ones at EUR 90,000, and art. 96 grades State-level fines (leves 301–30,000; graves 30,001–90,000; muy graves 90,001–1,000,000). Which figure applies to an online shop depends on the autonomous community's own typification (art. 78) or on sectoral legislation — not verified per region. The list of authorities designated by each autonomous community was not found in an official consolidated form; UTAC says a complaints procedure at its sede electrónica is 'próximamente' and contact is utac@dsca.gob.es. Ley 11/2023 DA 3ª: websites in scope must meet at least the medium level of generally recognised criteria, reference UNE 139803. Spain limits self-service terminals to 10 years (DT única 2) instead of the directive's 20.

act.title_original: Laki digitaalisten palvelujen tarjoamisesta (306/2019), 3 a luku
act.title_en: Act on the Provision of Digital Services (306/2019), chapter 3 a, added by Act 104/2023

penalties.summary_en: No fines: Traficom can order the service to be fixed within a reasonable time and back the order with a conditional fine (uhkasakko).

accessibility_information.where: stand-alone accessibility statement (saavutettavuusseloste); feedback answered within 2 weeks

transition: Service contracts made before 28 June 2025 may continue for up to 5 years.
notes: Supervision moved from the Regional State Administrative Agency for Southern Finland to Traficom on 1 Jan 2025.

act.title_original: LOI n° 2023-171 du 9 mars 2023 portant diverses dispositions d'adaptation au droit de l'Union européenne dans les domaines de l'économie, de la santé, du travail, des transports et de l'agriculture (art. 16)
act.title_en: Law No. 2023-171 of 9 March 2023 laying down various provisions adapting to European Union law in the fields of the economy, health, labour, transport and agriculture (Article 16)
act.citation: JORF n°0059 du 10 mars 2023 (NOR ECOX2229741L); EAA part codified in Code de la consommation art. L. 412-13 and L. 511-25-1

secondary_acts.title_original: Décret n° 2023-931 du 9 octobre 2023 relatif à l'accessibilité aux personnes handicapées des produits et services (Code de la consommation art. D. 412-49 à D. 412-62 et R. 451-4)
Arrêté du 9 octobre 2023 fixant les exigences en matière d'accessibilité applicables aux produits et services

authority_ecommerce.name_original: Direction générale de la concurrence, de la consommation et de la répression des fraudes (DGCCRF)
authority_ecommerce.name_en: Directorate-General for Competition Policy, Consumer Affairs and Fraud Control
authority_ecommerce.basis: Code de la consommation art. L. 511-25-1 (CCRF agents, plus sector regulators for telecoms/audiovisual/banking — none named for e-commerce); DGCCRF consumer information sheet on handicap.gouv.fr lists « le commerce électronique » among services it controls

penalties.summary_en: Each failure by a service provider (non-compliant service, missing/unpublished accessibility information, not informing authorities, not providing compliance information on request) is a 5th-class contravention: up to EUR 1,500 for a natural person and EUR 7,500 for a legal person per offence; repeat offences up to EUR 3,000 / EUR 15,000.
penalties.basis: Code de la consommation art. R. 451-4 I 10° and II; Code pénal art. 131-13 5°, 131-41, 132-11, 132-15

accessibility_information.basis: Code de la consommation art. D. 412-57 2° and its annex, I (« dans les clauses et conditions générales ou dans un document équivalent »)

microenterprise_exemption.basis: Code de la consommation art. L. 412-13 I, last paragraph (fewer than 10 persons and turnover or balance sheet ≤ EUR 2 million: exempt from the requirements and all related obligations)

transition: Until 28 June 2030 providers may keep using products they lawfully used before that date, and service contracts concluded before 28 June 2025 may run unchanged until they end, at the latest 28 June 2030 (loi n° 2023-171 art. 16 VIII B–C).
notes: Légifrance blocks scripted access (HTTP 403 to curl); codified articles L. 412-13, L. 511-25-1, D. 412-50, D. 412-57 + annex and R. 451-4 were read verbatim from the codes.droit.org consolidated Code de la consommation (DILA LEGI data, edition 2026-09-25); art. 16 VIII of the loi and the JORF numbers/NOR were read through a fetch tool that returns summaries of Légifrance pages, not raw text — its quote of VIII-C was internally inconsistent, so the '28 June 2025' contract cut-off follows the first fetch and Directive art. 32(1). max_amount is per contravention (legal person, first offence); fines are cumulative per offence. L. 412-13 applies « sans préjudice des articles 47 et 48 de la loi n° 2005-102 » — the separate digital-accessibility regime of art. 47 of loi 2005-102 (large companies) was not examined here.

penalties.summary_en: Administrative sanctions under the principle of proportionality; the act sets no amount for services (amounts are delegated to a presidential decree for products only).

transition: Contracts signed before 28 June 2025 may run up to 5 years (art. 28).
notes: The act names no market-surveillance authority for e-commerce services (art. 22(2) covers electronic communications only). Some secondary sources quote fines up to EUR 100,000 — not found in the act.

act.title_original: 2022. évi XVII. törvény a termékekre és a szolgáltatásokra vonatkozó akadálymentességi követelményeknek való megfelelés általános szabályairól (Aktv.)
act.title_en: Act XVII of 2022 on the general rules for compliance with accessibility requirements for products and services

authority_ecommerce.name_en: consumer protection authority (Budapest and county government offices)

penalties.summary_en: The authority first warns and agrees a deadline; a fine follows only if the business does not cooperate or fix. From HUF 15,000; up to HUF 500,000 for most businesses; for large non-SME businesses above HUF 100M turnover up to 5% of turnover, max HUF 500M.

transition: Service contracts signed before the act may run until they expire, at the latest 28 June 2030 (12. §).
notes: max_amount is the ceiling for large businesses; SMEs as a rule up to HUF 500,000.

act.title_original: Decreto legislativo 27 maggio 2022, n. 82 — Attuazione della direttiva (UE) 2019/882 del Parlamento europeo e del Consiglio, del 17 aprile 2019, sui requisiti di accessibilità dei prodotti e dei servizi
act.title_en: Legislative Decree No. 82 of 27 May 2022 — Implementation of Directive (EU) 2019/882 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 April 2019 on the accessibility requirements for products and services
act.citation: GU Serie Generale n. 152 del 1 luglio 2022 (22G00089)

secondary_acts.title_original: Linee guida AgID sull'accessibilità dei servizi in attuazione dell'art. 21 del decreto legislativo n. 82 del 2022 (adottate con Determinazione AgID n. 38/2026 del 4 marzo 2026)
secondary_acts.citation: Determinazione del Direttore generale AgID n. 38/2026, 4 marzo 2026 (pubblicata 5 marzo 2026)

secondary_acts.title_original: Legge 9 gennaio 2004, n. 4 — Disposizioni per favorire e semplificare l'accesso degli utenti e, in particolare, delle persone con disabilità agli strumenti informatici (art. 3, comma 1-bis; art. 9, comma 1-bis)

authority_ecommerce.basis: D.Lgs. 82/2022 art. 21, comma 1 and 3 (AgID « in qualità di Autorità di vigilanza sui servizi », incl. art. 1 c. 3 lett. f) e-commerce)

penalties.summary_en: A service provider that breaches the accessibility requirements or its service-provider obligations (art. 3, art. 12 c. 1–4) faces an administrative fine of EUR 5,000–40,000, graded by the extent of non-conformity and number of users affected; failure to comply with AgID corrective orders or to cooperate: EUR 2,500–30,000; providers with average turnover above EUR 500 million (L. 4/2004 art. 3 c. 1-bis) are in any case subject to the L. 4/2004 sanction of up to 5% of turnover.
penalties.basis: D.Lgs. 82/2022 art. 24, commi 1–3; L. 4/2004 art. 9, comma 1-bis

accessibility_information.basis: D.Lgs. 82/2022 art. 12, comma 2 and Allegato IV, punto 1 (« nelle condizioni generali, o in un documento equivalente »)

microenterprise_exemption.basis: D.Lgs. 82/2022 art. 3, comma 3 (definition art. 2 lett. bb): fewer than 10 persons and turnover or balance sheet ≤ EUR 2 million)

transition: Until 28 June 2030 providers may continue using products lawfully used before that date; service contracts concluded before 28 June 2025 may run unchanged until expiry but no longer than five years from that date (art. 25, comma 1).
notes: max_amount is the art. 24 c. 1 ceiling for ordinary providers; for providers with average turnover > EUR 500 million over the last three years, art. 24 c. 1 last sentence applies L. 4/2004 art. 9 c. 1-bis (AgID fine up to 5% of turnover after an unheeded warning), which has no fixed amount. Text read from the Normattiva consolidated version 'vigente al 25-9-2026' (art. 26 c. 2 repealed by L. 30 dicembre 2025, n. 199; art. 18 c. 6-bis and art. 25 c. 4-bis added later — none affect services' substantive rules). AgID guidelines (Det. 38/2026) not read in full.

act.title_original: Wet van 8 april 2024 tot wijziging van diverse wetten ter implementatie van Richtlijn (EU) 2019/882 (Implementatiewet toegankelijkheidsvoorschriften producten en diensten)
act.title_en: Act of 8 April 2024 amending various acts to implement Directive (EU) 2019/882 (Accessibility Requirements for Products and Services Implementation Act)
act.citation: Stb. 2024, 87; entry into force Stb. 2024, 341. E-commerce rules inserted as Burgerlijk Wetboek Boek 6, art. 230fa–230fd (Afdeling 2ab)

authority_ecommerce.name_en: Netherlands Authority for Consumers and Markets (ACM)
authority_ecommerce.basis: Wet handhaving consumentenbescherming art. 2.2 with Bijlage onderdeel a (lists art. 8.15, 8a.0, 8a.1 Whc); art. 8.15 Whc (e-commerce provider must comply with BW 6:230fb). AFM instead of ACM for financial services.

penalties.type: administrative fine and/or periodic penalty payment (last onder dwangsom)
penalties.summary_en: Breach of BW 6:230fb (via art. 8.15 Whc) is an infringement for which the ACM may impose an order subject to periodic penalty or an administrative fine of up to EUR 900,000 or, if higher, 1% of the offender's turnover (doubled for a repeat offence within five years).
penalties.basis: art. 2.9 and 2.15(1), (4) Wet handhaving consumentenbescherming; art. 8.15 Whc; BW 6:230fb

accessibility_information.where: statute: information per Annex V of Directive (EU) 2019/882 (i.e. general terms and conditions or equivalent document); ACM guidance: an accessibility statement (verklaring) on the website/app, easy to find, itself accessible, in written and oral form

microenterprise_exemption.basis: BW 6:230fc(1) (art. 230fb does not apply to undertakings with fewer than 10 employees and annual turnover or balance sheet total ≤ EUR 2 million)

transition: Afdeling 2ab does not apply to e-commerce services performed before it entered into force; providers may keep using products they lawfully used until 27 June 2030, and contracts concluded via e-commerce services before 28 June 2025 may run unchanged until expiry, at most five years (art. 190aa Overgangswet nieuw Burgerlijk Wetboek; art. VIII(4) Implementatiewet excludes e-commerce from the Act's general transitional rule).
notes: The statute itself does not use the word 'toegankelijkheidsverklaring'; it refers to Annex V of the Directive. The 'verklaring op website/app' is ACM's reading. ACM's page states the scope as '10 or more employees, or turnover above EUR 2 million, or both', which matches the statute (exempt only if BOTH <10 employees AND ≤ EUR 2 million turnover or balance sheet total). Art. 190aa(2) OBW and art. VIII(1) Implementatiewet as published read 'vóór 28 juni 2030' (probably a drafting slip for 2025; quoted as published). The Staatsblad metadata wrongly dates the Act '8 april 2023'; the Act itself says 8 April 2024. The Whc fine regime lets ACM take account of turnover; the 4% / EUR 2 million CPC-coordinated-action cap in art. 2.15(3) does not list art. 8.15. No NL implementing decree specific to e-commerce services was found (decrees exist for e-books, audiovisual, transport, banking, electronic communications).

act.title_original: Ustawa z dnia 26 kwietnia 2024 r. o zapewnianiu spełniania wymagań dostępności niektórych produktów i usług przez podmioty gospodarcze
act.title_en: Act of 26 April 2024 on ensuring compliance with accessibility requirements of certain products and services by economic operators

authority_ecommerce.name_original: Minister właściwy do spraw informatyzacji (Minister Cyfryzacji); ponadto Prezes Zarządu PFRON (kontrola, postępowania, kary)
authority_ecommerce.name_en: Minister responsible for computerisation (Minister of Digital Affairs); in addition the President of the Management Board of the State Fund for Rehabilitation of Disabled Persons (PFRON) can inspect and fine
authority_ecommerce.basis: art. 38 ust. 2 i ust. 3 pkt 2; art. 39; art. 73 ust. 3

penalties.summary_en: A service provider that fails to ensure accessibility, to carry out the conformity assessment, to inform the authority of non-compliance, or to supply information on request can be fined up to ten times the average monthly wage in the national economy for the previous year, but not more than 10% of the previous year's turnover.

accessibility_information.where: terms of service (regulamin) or other equivalent document
accessibility_information.basis: art. 32 ust. 2 pkt 1 (« w regulaminie świadczenia usług lub innym równoważnym dokumencie »), art. 33

transition: Service contracts concluded before 28 June 2025 may remain in force unchanged until they expire but no later than 28 June 2030, and providers may use non-compliant products they used before that date until 28 June 2030 (art. 85 ust. 1–2).
notes: max_amount = 10 × PLN 8,903.56 (average wage in the national economy in 2025, Komunikat Prezesa GUS z 9 lutego 2026 r., M.P. 2026 poz. 192, issued under the FUS pensions act as art. 73 requires), so it applies to fines imposed in 2026 and changes every year; the 10%-of-turnover cap can make it lower. Brief's starting point (PFRON as the authority) is only partly right: the market surveillance authority for e-commerce is the minister for computerisation; PFRON's President monitors the system, receives notifications (art. 67) and may also inspect and fine. penalties.summary_en: For legal persons: EUR 12,000–24,000 for a grave offence, from EUR 24,000 up to the general statutory ceiling for a very grave one (non-compliant service = very grave); halved limits for negligence; convictions are published.

transition: Service contracts concluded before the act came into force are exempt until 28 June 2030 (art. 38.º).
